claim_verdicts.evidence: Glossary: "The API server is the front end for the Kubernetes control plane." kubernetes-api.md: "Users, the different parts of your cluster, and external components all communicate with one another through the API server." control-plane-node-communication.md: "The API server is configured to listen for remote connections on a secure HTTPS port (typically 443)".
Glossary kubectl: "Command line tool for communicating with a Kubernetes cluster's control plane, using the Kubernetes API."

"By default, `kubectl` looks for a file named `config` in the `$HOME/.kube` directory. You can specify other kubeconfig files by setting the `KUBECONFIG` environment variable or by setting the `--kubeconfig` flag." Lesson omits --kubeconfig; not wrong for the scope. Executed -v=6: "Config loaded from file: C:\Users\...\.kube\config".

Captured output outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/cluster-up.txt@stage-2: "Set kubectl context to \"kind-donhang\"". kind Quick Start (WebFetch summary): "kubectl cluster-info --context kind-kind" / "kind-kind-2" (pattern kind-<name>); "the cluster access configuration is stored in ${HOME}/.kube/config if $KUBECONFIG environment variable is not set." Executed `kubectl config current-context` -> kind-donhang.

Executed `kubectl config view --minify`: "server: https://127.0.0.1:51407", "client-certificate-data: DATA+OMITTED", "client-key-data: DATA+OMITTED". `docker port donhang-control-plane`: "6443/tcp -> 127.0.0.1:51407". kind configuration docs (WebFetch summary): "By default the API server listens on a random open port."; keep apiServerAddress "the default (127.0.0.1) for security reasons."
claim_verdicts.source: executed (kubectl v1.34.3, kind v0.33.0); github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind site/content/docs/user/configuration.md

claim_verdicts.evidence: Executed `kubectl get nodes -v=6`: "Response" verb="GET" url="https://127.0.0.1:51407/api/v1/nodes?limit=500" status="200 OK". api-concepts.md shows the same chunked-list form "GET /api/v1/pods?limit=500". Note: the claim says nothing about the number of requests; see issues for "one HTTP request".

node-status.md: "The kubelet is responsible for creating and updating the `.status` of Nodes, and for updating their related Leases." nodes.md: "--node-status-update-frequency - Specifies how often kubelet posts its node status to the API server." Hub-and-spoke: "All API usage from nodes (or the pods they run) terminates at the API server." ... "secure HTTPS port".

Executed `kubectl config current-context -v=6`: only "kubectl command headers turned on" and "Config loaded from file: ...\.kube\config" log lines, then "kind-donhang"; no "Response" line, i.e. no HTTP request.
claim_verdicts.source: executed kubectl v1.34.3 against cluster donhang

claim_verdicts.evidence: `git show stage-2:scripts/k8s/get-nodes.sh` lines 5-12 match the lesson block character-for-character (show(), lesson marker, two comment lines, current-context, echo, get nodes). outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/get-nodes.txt matches the text block exactly, AGE already masked as "..." by outputs/unstable.regex.

Executed `kubectl get nodes --show-labels`: only donhang-control-plane carries node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane=, and only it shows ROLES control-plane; workers show <none>. Docs: "Kubernetes defines one specific node role, control-plane. A label you can use to mark that node role is node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane." (Docs do not describe how kubectl builds ROLES; established by execution.)

Executed `kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=N:.metadata.name,V:.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion`: all three nodes v1.34.11, identical to the VERSION column; node image kindest/node:v1.34.11 pinned in deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml@stage-2.

Docs: "`--v=6` | Display requested resources." Round 2, executed on kind-donhang: `kubectl get nodes -v=6 2>&1 | grep nodes` -> one line: "Response" verb="GET" url="https://127.0.0.1:51407/api/v1/nodes?limit=500" status="200 OK". With an empty --cache-dir: `grep -c Response` = 3 (/api, /apis, /api/v1/nodes), `grep nodes` still exactly one line. Without 2>&1 the log lines do not reach grep (stderr).

access-cluster.md: "To access a cluster, you need to know the location of the cluster and have credentials to access it." control-plane-node-communication.md: API server "is configured to listen for remote connections on a secure HTTPS port". Nothing requires kubectl to run on a node.

Executed (cluster not stopped, per instructions) `kubectl --server=https://127.0.0.1:1 get nodes` against an address with nothing listening: "Unable to connect to the server: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connectex: No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it." Stopping the node containers removes the 127.0.0.1:51407 port mapping (docker port), giving the same failure.
claim_verdicts.source: executed kubectl v1.34.3; docker port donhang-control-plane

claim_verdicts.evidence: controlling-access.md: "Authentication modules include client certificates, password, and plain tokens" ... "If the request cannot be authenticated, it is rejected with HTTP status code 401." Executed curl to the kind API server with `Authorization: Bearer bogus`: Status "reason": "Unauthorized", "code": 401; with no credentials: 403.

kubectl config view reference: --minify "Remove all information not used by current-context from the output"; --raw "Display raw byte data and sensitive data". Executed on kind-donhang: `kubectl config view --minify` shows only cluster/context/user kind-donhang with client-certificate-data and client-key-data as DATA+OMITTED; with --raw, client-key-data is printed as base64 data.

issues.text: Title (from track.yaml) still overstates: `kubectl config current-context` (section 5, claim 8) sends no request, so not every kubectl command is a request. Body and summary are now correctly scoped. Left to the owner; not blocking.
issues.quote: Every kubectl command is a request to the API server
issues.fix: Owner decision via outline edit: e.g. "Every kubectl command that touches the cluster is a request to the API server" or "kubectl talks to the cluster through the API server".
